statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with Corporations Canada within 30 days of rejection notice, providing supporting documentation; appeal granted if name is not confusing or objectionable under section 12 of CBCA

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), accessible via the CRA My Business Account portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain a Business Number (BN) upon incorporation. Foreign entities register with the CRA to procure a BN as their statutory tax identification number (TIN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; Canadian corporations are subject to entity-level taxation under the Income Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch election rules apply under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically via the CRA's My Business Account system. Real-time reporting is required for certain large businesses under the GST/HST Modernization; digital clearance through API integrations for high-volume filers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services performed outside Canada are zero-rated for GST/HST purposes provided the exporter or service provider meets the criteria under section 2 of the Excise Tax Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent claims for zero-rating may result in penalties of up to 50% of the tax evaded, plus interest; retrospective adjustments and potential prosecution under the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central monetary authority issuing the CAD and overseeing financial system stability); OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) regulates and supervises federally chartered banks and foreign bank branches; the Investment Review Division of ISED administers the Investment Canada Act. FINTRAC implements federal AML/CFT transaction reporting and MSB registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates under a free-floating currency regime with no separate exchange control law and no distinction between capital and current account convertibility for routine business transactions. Profit remittance, dividends, and loan interest may be freely repatriated subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds (C$10,000 for cross-border currency transfers) and documentary proof of the underlying commercial purpose. Investment Canada Act net benefit review may apply to acquisitions of control of Canadian businesses, but it does not restrict ongoing repatriation of earnings. Non-resident taxes under the Income Tax Act (Part XIII or treaty reductions) govern remittance mechanics, not availability of foreign exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose any statutory export proceeds surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted to CAD at the exporter's discretion, provided the reporting entity files electronic transaction reports with FINTRAC when inflows cross the C$10,000 threshold and, for customs-related trade data, reports via the Canada Border Services Agency and Statistics Canada in accordance with the International Merchandise Trade Data requirements. No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High with regulatory qualification. A foreign fintech/EMI without a Canadian banking license may not accept demand deposits or offer banking products but can operate as a Money Services Business (MSB) registered with FINTRAC, subject to registration before conducting business in Canada. Cross-border digital banks or EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, or EU/UK EMIs) may support inbound CAD settlement through partner banks, but they cannot provide Canadian domestic clearing access unless they hold deposits at a Payment Service Provider regulated and the partner conducts the clearing. Legal constraints include the Bank Act prohibition on the use of the word 'bank' without incorporation under the Bank Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations requiring wind-down of accounts if FINTRAC registration lapses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for a federally incorporated corporation provided that corporate identification documents are notarized or certified by a notary public in the director's jurisdiction and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s) pass a remote video verification. The individual directors and signatories do not need to physically appear at a Canadian branch, but the bank may impose a heightened requirement for first-time foreign nationals: the signing officer must complete a live video conference call with the Relationship Manager. Physical presence is mandatory only when the foreign corporate structure involves a high-risk country, when the account cannot be opened through a standard electronic KYC, or when the bank's internal policy overrides the federal guidance. Certain Tier 1 banks accept fully digital onboarding using TrustID/Experian-level verification in conjunction with apostilled corporate registry documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial owner chain with anonymous shell companies or trusts in non-cooperative jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart listing every intermediate vehicle from ultimate principals to the Canadian entity; certified registry extracts with full ownership register (updated within 30 days); declaration of nominal ownership / non-disclosure trust arrangement (if applicable); and a written explanation of the syndicated newswire revenue model demonstrating a genuine commercial nexus to Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity coded as 'financial news aggregation' triggering potential money services business (MSB) or securities dealer concerns under supervision
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming that the ISIC 6391 / NAICS 519110 news syndication feed does not constitute a payment service, deposit-taking, or securities dealing activity; the contractual API distribution agreements; FINTRAC risk assessment self-review; and confirmation that no 'clearing and settlement' of client funds occurs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume expected cross-border wire movement inconsistent with low-risk revenue profile or thin corporate capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements (if available) or a board-approved treasury forecast; executed subscription agreements from corporate clients; projected invoice flows demonstrating that inbound wires tie to API news feed licence fees; and evidence of shareholder equity capital provided from regulated financial institutions in Canada, Europe, or the US.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or UBOs resident in a high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., FATF grey-list country) or appearing on restricted sanctions lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Police clearance certificates / criminal records from each jurisdiction of residence issued within 90 days; adverse media search report; a sworn affidavit of biography documenting source of wealth and source of funds for equity contributions; and a detailed business rationale including client contracts with supply-chain finance transacting only with permissible counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital assets, cryptocurrency, or unstable lines of credit to fund initial capital contributions, unable to verify origination
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements (last 12 months) of the contributing shareholder showing original clearing source; certified confirmation from the contributing bank that the funds are drawn from a regulated account; conversion reports from crypto exchange showing fiat on/off ramp; and a notarized share subscription certificate with consideration paid in lawful fiat currency only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign investment into the Canadian federal corporation should be executed via SWIFT MT103 through a Tier 1 correspondent bank. The wire instruction must include: (1) Purpose code consistent with the Canadian FX requirement—typically 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' or 'Intercompany Loan (foreign affiliate)'; banks accept the ITSMT104/MT103 field 70 (Remittance Information) and field 72 (Bank-to-Bank Info) to state 'PAYMENT FOR SHARE ISSUANCE' or 'LOAN PRINCIPAL PER LOAN AGREEMENT DATED YYYY-MM-DD'. For equity contributions above C$1,000,000, provide the bank with a certified copy of the federal certificate of incorporation, a share subscription agreement, and a board resolution; the bank will classify the inflow as direct investment and not as a transfer for clearing purposes. To ensure the rate is transparent, request a pre-arranged CAD/USD conversion with a forward contract or spot at the bank's wholesale desk; if the funds are received in a non-CAD currency, the bank may automatically convert them at the prevailing rate and report the transaction under the Foreign Currency Denominated Account program. If funds arrive from a related party in the US / Europe, ensure compliance with Part XIII thin capitalization and transfer pricing rules by filing a contemporaneous loan documentation set with the bank for the account opening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for syndicated finance/news subscription or trade settlements may be routed via Payments Canada's High Value Clearing System (HVCS) or Lynx (the final settlement system for large-value Canadian dollars) when using domestic clearing. For international vendor payments and trade settlement, use SWIFT MT103 with a due date matched to the invoice and supporting the documentary requirement; for letters of credit, use an irrevocable commercial LC (UCP600) confirmed by a Canadian Tier 1 bank, with MT700 transmitted to the beneficiary's bank. For payments in USD, Canadian banks typically route via the United States clearing network (ACH/Fedwire) through their US correspondent; in this case, the wire must include the CUSIP, reference of the underlying transaction, and the Canadian bank's CHIPS/ABA identifier. All outbound wires above C$10,000 are subject to FINTRAC reporting and must include the purpose code 'Consulting/Subscriptions/Intangible Service' as appropriate. For subscription fees paid to content licensors outside Canada, do not use cheques; direct debits or credit card rails are permissible for smaller amounts, but the API distribution model requires regular monthly or quarterly SWIFT transfers with a standing instruction and an active Automated Clearing Settlement (ACS) code from the receiving institution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (non-deliverable, market-standard in Canada for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) entered into with a Schedule I bank or an OSFI-regulated dealer
FX swaps (CAD vs. USD) with same-day or short-tenor settlement cleared through CIBC, RBC, or TD's treasury desk, using the Canadian Foreign Exchange Committee prevailing documentation

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge underlying loan or bond funding, provided the swap is executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with a swap credit support annex, and cleared through a regulated CCP where applicable
FX options (vanilla calls/puts) on major currencies, purchased for hedging projected trade disbursement or subscription fee exposure, with non-dealer end-user exemption from mandatory clearing

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) are permissible only for currencies not freely deliverable (e.g., certain emerging-market currencies underlying the syndicated finance newswire's hedge fund client base), but the Canadian bank will require a physical ISDDA/CSA and the NDF will be cash-settled in USD, not CAD; NDFs for CAD is not standard.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science, and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date, irrespective of fiscal period; online filing is available through the Corporations Canada portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100 after the 60-day deadline; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212 and escheat of assets to the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the taxation year-end (fiscal period-end); for a Canadian-controlled private corporation, the income tax balance is due within 3 months after year-end; for other corporations, within 2 months.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; interest is charged at the CRA prescribed rate; repeated non-filing may trigger a deemed assessment or prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ISC (Individuals with Significant Control) Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual return within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary; the Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be updated within 15 days of any change in control or share transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of the ISC Register is an offence punishable on summary conviction: fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or 6 months imprisonment for individuals; fines up to CAD 1,000,000 for corporations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of an auditor is mandatory for distributing (public) corporations. A non-distributing private federal corporation is exempt when annual gross revenues are CAD 1,000,000 or less OR total assets at fiscal year-end are CAD 1,000,000 or less; the exemption is lost if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares requisition an audit, and a unanimous shareholder resolution may waive the audit only where the exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is required for distributing corporations; non-listed private corporations may apply ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) or consistently adopt IFRS; all financial statements must comply with Part X of the CBCA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA ss. 21.1-21.45, a federal corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) identifying any person with 25% or greater ownership, share entitlement, or influence. The register must be created within 15 days of incorporation, updated within 15 days of any change (including share transfers), and its existence and content confirmed annually through the annual return. The register is open to inspection by shareholders under prescribed conditions and by certain enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)
Central Securities Register recording all share issuances and transfers
Minute Book containing annual general meeting minutes, director minutes, and written resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,150 per year (CAD 400 - 1,500) for registered corporate office or registered agent services provider fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 22,500 (CAD 8,000 - 30,000) for a typical non-listed private federal corporation statutory audit; a review engagement generally ranges from USD 2,500 - 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% general federal corporate rate after provincial abatement (38% statutory rate less 10% provincial abatement and 13% general reduction); provincial corporate rates add 0% to 16% depending on province of permanent establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: 9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; SR&ED investment tax credits; general rate reduction for manufacturing and processing; clean technology and innovation investment tax credits; foreign tax credit for cross-border taxation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) E-file (EFILE), approved third-party software, or CRA My Business Account portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly tax installments are required when the total tax liability exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due date is no later than 6 months after the taxation year-end; final balance-due remittance is due within 2 months after the tax year-end for most corporations, or within 3 months for qualifying CCPCs with business income below the small business deduction limit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, business number (BN/RT), jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal period end date, amalgamation or winding-up status, and non-resident indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on a business in Canada must report its Canadian business number and federal tax year-end; identify the permanent establishment location and filing status in the relevant boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 100 - Gross Revenue and Operating Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from financial news aggregation, syndicated finance feeds, API subscriptions, and other income streams, excluding dividends and interest collected separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source gross revenue attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment or, in the absence of a PE, income taxable under Part XIV of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue after cost of goods sold, operating expenses, salaries, corporate overhead, interest expense, technology infrastructure costs, and amortization; adjustments for items such as over-/under-allowances are reported.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only expenses that are reasonable and directly allocable to the Canadian PE and supported by transfer-pricing documentation; cross-border cost allocations must be made on an arm's length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after application of non-capital loss carryovers, capital gains exemptions, preferred-rate amounts, and foreign income tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers may deduct the same available losses and carryovers to the extent they are attributable to the Canadian PE; treaty sourcing rules limit what income is recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 - Net Federal Provision / Line 550 - Federal Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal income tax at the 15% general rate after provincial abatement, including small business deduction and manufacturing/general rate reductions, and any special credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations allocate federal tax among provinces via permanent establishments; the calculation must use the provincial allocation formula for the province where income is earned.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s.162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full late month up to 12 months; repeated failure increases to 10% plus 2% per month. Failure to remit installments and non-electronic filing may trigger additional penalties; unpaid taxes and penalties accrue daily compound arrears interest charged by the CRA.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on lump-sum dividends, deemed dividends, and dividends paid or credited to non-resident recipients; treaty rates often reduce this to 5% for substantial corporate shareholders and 15% for portfolio investments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must obtain an official Certificate of Residency (TRC) from its home tax authority and provide it to the Canadian payer; a completed and timely Form NR301 (Claim for Reduced Treaty Withholding) must be submitted to the CRA (or the payer) before the payment date. The payer must then reduce the statutory withholding rate in accordance with the applicable DTA. Retroactive treaty relief is available through an income-tax-refund claim within two years of filing the T2 return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate is 25% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents; Comprehensive tax treaties may reduce interest to 0-10% and royalties to 0-10%, depending on treaty terms and beneficial-ownership conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No formal numeric threshold is fixed by statute; however, CRA's contemporaneous documentation guidance generally anticipates a full Master File and Local File for non-resident intercompany transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate value. Simpler documentation may satisfy lower-risk or smaller-dollar obligors, but all cross-border transactions with non-arm's length parties must be priced at arm's length under s.247.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to UAE ESR; instead, the CRA applies the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under s.245 to transactions lacking genuine commercial substance, and relies on the beneficial-ownership requirement and the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal-purpose test to deny treaty benefits for conduit or shell structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully failing to report Canadian-source revenue from syndicated finance news feeds, issuing false invoices to foreign affiliates, or destroying books and records to conceal taxable cash flows through payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.238(1): fine up to CAD 50,000 plus 200% of the amount of tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 2 years; criminal prosecution under the Criminal Code s.380 for fraudulent receipt of funds can impose up to 10 years imprisonment. CRA additionally applies gross-negligence penalties under s.163(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who directed, assented to, or acquiesced in the evasion may be personally liable for the corporate tax arrears through penalty notices, and are subject to civil restitution, imprisonment, and travel bans if charged under the Criminal Code; the corporate veil may be pierced to recover misappropriated assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Part XIII Tax on Outbound Dividends, Royalties, or Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident corporate parent or shareholder without deducting, reporting, or remitting the 25% statutory withholding tax, or without valid treaty relief documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The non-resident withholding amount remains payable in full, plus a 10% penalty under s.227(8), daily compound interest, and additional fines up to CAD 1,000 or CAD 25,000 for subsequent offences under Part XIII.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be made jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding amounts under s.227.1 if they did not exercise due diligence; they can face personal bank account seizures, notices of assessment in their capacity, travel restrictions, and criminal liability if the omission is fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Documentation Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling financial news data, API access, or syndication services to a foreign affiliate at a low margin without contemporaneous Canadian transfer-pricing documentation, or failing to demonstrate a reasonable arm's length effort.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 247(3) imposes a 10% penalty on the net transfer-pricing adjustment whenever the understated corporate income or overstated tax-account loss exceeds CAD 1,000,000; the primary amount can be reassessed for the applicable taxation year, and interest runs from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Although transfer-pricing penalties generally attach to the corporation, directors who sign false or misleading documentation can incur personal gross-negligence penalties under s.163.2 and, where fraud is shown, criminal sanctions; courts may order restitution from directors who knowingly caused under-reporting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Shopping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an offshore-affiliated Canadian corporation with no employees, premises, or substantive business activities solely to access reduced DTA withholding rates and channel dividends or capital gains to a tax-haven parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under s.245(2) disallows the avoidance transaction and restores taxes as if the transaction did not occur; treaty benefits are denied under the principal-purpose test; the CRA may impose gross-negligence penalties and revoke non-resident withholding relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who establish or manage a hollow company for treaty abuse face personal assessment under GAAR-related reassessment plus possible false-statements prosecution, travel bans, and 10-year imprisonment if cross-border funds are laundered or fraudulent misrepresentation is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Swift Wire, Stripe, or other payment rails to receive and distribute large news-subscription and syndication payments without registering with FINTRAC, performing CDD/KYC, verifying beneficial ownership, or maintaining suspicious-transaction reporting controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) administrative penalties can reach CAD 500,000 for a first failure-to-report violation; criminal anti-money-laundering offences carry fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years. The CRA may also impose separate tax penalties for unrecorded cash-equivalent wire receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are subject to FINTRAC cease-porto penalties and personal criminal liability when they knowingly permitted unregistered money services; concurrent CRA and civil-forfeiture proceedings may seize personal assets, impose restitution, and ban travel for non-cooperation.
